title: Anonymous Closure Types
goal: Learn that every closure has a unique anonymous type generated by the compiler.

sections.text: In languages like Python or JavaScript, lambda functions share a standard function type. In Rust, every closure definition produces its own unique, unnamable struct type.

sections.caption: Identical closure expressions still create distinct types.

sections.text: Because two closures never share the same concrete type, you cannot store them both in a standard `Vec` under a single generic type parameter. You must erase their types.

sections.code:
let list: Vec<Box<dyn Fn(i32) -> i32>> =
    vec![Box::new(f), Box::new(g)];
sections.caption: Box<dyn Fn(...)> unifies distinct closure types behind a trait object.

sections.text: If a closure captures no variables, it can also coerce to a plain function pointer like `fn(i32) -> i32`. Function pointers do not require heap allocation.

explanation: Learn that every closure has a unique anonymous type generated by the compiler.
